A student investigates the temperature change when anhydrous lithium chloride dissolves in
water.
The student does five experiments.
Experiment 1
Use a 50 cm3 measuring cylinder to pour 40 cm3 of distilled water into a 100 cm3 beaker.
•
•
Use a thermometer to measure the initial temperature of the water.
•
Add a 2.0 g sample of anhydrous lithium chloride to the water in the beaker.
•
Continually stir the mixture in the beaker using the thermometer.
•
Measure the highest temperature reached by the mixture in the beaker.
•
Empty the beaker and rinse the beaker with distilled water.
Experiment 2
Repeat Experiment 1 using 30 cm3 of distilled water instead of 40 cm3.
•
Experiment 3
Repeat Experiment 1 using 25 cm3 of distilled water instead of 40 cm3.
•
Experiment 4
Repeat Experiment 1 using 20 cm3 of distilled water instead of 40 cm3.
•
Experiment 5
Repeat Experiment 1 using 15 cm3 of distilled water instead of 40 cm3.
•
